Questions.Question: When soldering radio circuits, what safety precaution should be taken regarding chemical fumes?

Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.7, p. 300

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Under ComReg Guidelines 09/45, how must station equipment be identified and labelled?

Only the main antenna feedline needs a red danger tag
All controls, meters, and terminals must be clearly labelled with manufacturer trademark, type, and serial number

Questions.Explanation: ComReg regulations require clear labelling of controls, terminals, power supply details, manufacturer trademark, model, and serial number.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: For a 100W HF dipole at 7 MHz, what is the key factor in ensuring general public exposure stays below ICNIRP limits?

Using a lower loss coaxial cable
Mounting the antenna at adequate height and ensuring minimum physical separation

Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.8.5, p. 309
Questions.Explanation: Public compliance is primarily achieved by positioning the antenna high enough and far enough away so people cannot enter the high-field reactive near zone.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What simple measure can help prevent mains power lines from conducting RF interference into an amateur transceiver?
Options: Fitting a mains RF line filter with ferrite chokes
Connecting a variable capacitor across the live and neutral wires
Removing the earth pin from the mains plug
Questions.Correct answer: Fitting a mains RF line filter with ferrite chokes
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 18.1.5, p. 286
Questions.Explanation: Mains RF line filters stop conducted RF energy from entering or leaving equipment via electrical supply lines.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What directive ensures that commercial electrical equipment sold in the EU possesses adequate immunity and low emissions?

Questions.Explanation: The EU Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) Directive and Radio Equipment Directive (RED) require CE-marked products to meet emission and immunity standards.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the effect of FM over-deviation in a transmitter?
Options: Immediate destruction of the antenna balun
Reduced audio output at the receiver
Excessive bandwidth occupation causing adjacent channel interference (splatter)
Questions.Correct answer: Excessive bandwidth occupation causing adjacent channel interference (splatter)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 11.4.2, p. 155 & Ch 18.2, p. 289
Questions.Explanation: Exceeding the permitted peak frequency deviation expands the transmitted FM bandwidth beyond limits, spilling into adjacent channels.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Where does intermodulation distortion (IMD) primarily originate in a receiver?
Options: In the DC power supply bridge rectifier
In non-linear stages such as mixers or overdriven RF amplifiers when two strong signals mix
In the audio speaker voice coil
Questions.Correct answer: In non-linear stages such as mixers or overdriven RF amplifiers when two strong signals mix
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.7.8, p. 205 & Ch 18.2, p. 288
Questions.Explanation: Intermodulation occurs when two or more strong out-of-band signals mix in non-linear receiver stages (RF amp/mixer) to produce phantom signals.

Questions.Question: What orientation of electric field lines defines vertical wave polarization?

Electric field lines parallel to the Earth's surface
Magnetic field lines vertical to the Earth's surface

Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 7.8, p. 86 & Ch 15.6, p. 229
Questions.Explanation: Wave polarization is defined by the direction of the E-field vector. Vertical polarization has E-field lines standing perpendicular to the ground.

Questions.Question: What formula expresses Ohm's law to calculate resistance when voltage (V) and current (I) are known?

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: According to Carson's Rule, what is the total bandwidth required for an FM voice transmission?

Equal to the peak frequency deviation Δf
Twice the highest modulating audio frequency
Questions.Correct answer: Twice the sum of peak frequency deviation and highest modulating audio frequency: BW = 2*(Δf + fmax)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 11.4.2, p. 155 / Sample Exam Q20
Questions.Explanation: Carson's Rule states FM bandwidth BW ≈ 2 * (Peak Deviation + Max Audio Frequency).

Questions.Question: What buffer stage is placed after a master oscillator in a transmitter?

Questions.Explanation: A buffer amplifier provides high input impedance to prevent downstream amplifier loading from pulling or shifting the oscillator frequency.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What detector is specifically used in receivers to demodulate SSB and CW signals?

Questions.Question: If a transmission feedline must run close to metallic structures or building walls, which feedline type should be used?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 14.6, p. 211 / Sample Exam Q22

After the low-pass filter and after the antenna tuner
Between the microphone and transceiver input
Directly at the antenna feed point outdoors

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What device converts unbalanced coaxial feedline current to balanced current for feeding a dipole antenna?

Questions.Question: What is the front-to-back ratio of a directional Yagi antenna?
Options: The ratio of boom length to element diameter
The ratio of power radiated in the main forward lobe to power radiated in the opposite reverse direction (expressed in dB)
The ratio of input impedance to output impedance
The ratio of total height to ground reflection
Questions.Correct answer: The ratio of power radiated in the main forward lobe to power radiated in the opposite reverse direction (expressed in dB)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 15.16, p. 248
Questions.Explanation: Front-to-back ratio compares radiation intensity in the desired forward direction versus 180° directly behind it.

Questions.Question: What causes signal 'fading' (QSB) on HF skywave contacts?

Questions.Correct answer: Interference between multiple skywave paths arriving out of phase (multipath fading)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.9, p. 269
Questions.Explanation: Multipath propagation causes signals arriving over slightly different path lengths or polarizations to constructively and destructively interfere.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is Earth-Moon-Earth (EME) propagation?

Communicating with lunar astronauts on HF 80m
Using the Moon as a passive reflector for extreme long-distance VHF/UHF/microwave communications
Reflecting HF ground waves off ocean tides
Questions.Correct answer: Using the Moon as a passive reflector for extreme long-distance VHF/UHF/microwave communications
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.8.8, p. 268
Questions.Explanation: EME (Moonbounce) uses high-power directive antennas to reflect VHF/UHF signals off the surface of the Moon back to Earth.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Why does a lower radiation angle (takeoff angle) from an HF antenna increase communication distance?
Options: Lower takeoff angles increase transmitter ERP by 6 dB
Lower takeoff angles bypass the ionosphere completely
Lower takeoff angles hit the ionosphere further out, producing longer single-hop skip distances
Lower takeoff angles eliminate multipath fading
Questions.Correct answer: Lower takeoff angles hit the ionosphere further out, producing longer single-hop skip distances
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.7, p. 265
Questions.Explanation: Low takeoff angles strike the ionospheric refracting layer closer to the horizon, expanding the ground distance per hop.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What ionospheric layer exists only during daylight hours and splits into two distinct sub-layers (F1 and F2)?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.3.3, p. 259
Questions.Explanation: During the day, intense solar radiation splits the F-layer into F1 (~200 km) and F2 (~400 km) layers.

Questions.Question: What instrument displays RF signal amplitude across a visual frequency domain axis?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 17.5, p. 278
Questions.Explanation: A spectrum analyzer plots signal strength on the vertical axis against frequency on the horizontal axis.

To check transmitter power amplifier linearity and detect intermodulation distortion/flat-topping

Transmitting a CQ call to inform other stations

Keep one hand behind your back
Questions.Correct answer: Keep one hand behind your back
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.3, p. 293 & Ch 19.4.6, p. 299
Questions.Explanation: Keeping one hand behind your back prevents forming a current path across the chest cavity between two hands.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Guy ropes supporting a guyed antenna mast should be secured to the ground at what minimum distance from the base?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.6.1, p. 299 / Sample Exam Q4
Questions.Explanation: Engineering best practice specifies securing guy anchors 60% to 80% of the total mast height away from the base.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is cross-modulation in a receiver?
Options: The conversion of AM signals to FM in the detector
The mixing of IF frequencies with the local oscillator
The modulation of a desired weak signal by an unwanted strong modulating signal in a non-linear stage
The reflection of signals from ionospheric E-layers
Questions.Correct answer: The modulation of a desired weak signal by an unwanted strong modulating signal in a non-linear stage
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.7.9, p. 205
Questions.Explanation: Cross-modulation occurs when the modulation from an undesired strong signal transfers onto the carrier of a desired weak signal inside a non-linear RF stage.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What causes key clicks in a CW transmission?
Options: Transmitting CW on an SSB frequency
Unfiltered keying waveforms with excessively steep rise and fall times
Using a mechanical Morse key instead of an electronic keyer
Questions.Correct answer: Unfiltered keying waveforms with excessively steep rise and fall times
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 11.8.1, p. 160 & Ch 18.2, p. 288
Questions.Explanation: Abrupt switching of the RF carrier produces very sharp rise/fall times, generating broad sideband pulses known as key clicks.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What unwanted emissions are produced by a transmitter outside its allocated operating bandwidth?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 18.2.1, p. 290
Questions.Explanation: Spurious emissions include harmonics, parasitic oscillations, and intermodulation products outside the permitted transmission bandwidth.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is 'desensitisation' in a radio receiver?
Options: The loss of sensitivity due to low battery voltage
The audio distortion occurring during SSB reception
The thermal noise generated in an un-tuned antenna
A reduction in receiver gain caused by a strong nearby off-frequency signal overloading the front end
Questions.Correct answer: A reduction in receiver gain caused by a strong nearby off-frequency signal overloading the front end
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.7.7, p. 205
Questions.Explanation: Desensitisation (blocking) occurs when a very strong off-frequency signal drives receiver AGC or RF stages into gain reduction.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: By what factor does power increase when a power ratio is stated as +3 dB?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 9.1, p. 117
Questions.Explanation: A 3 dB power increase represents a doubling of power (+3 dB = x2 power).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: What power is dissipated in a 5 ohm resistor when a current of 10 A flows through it?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 3.10.1, p. 23 / Sample Exam Q10

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: What formula expresses Ohm's law to calculate resistance when voltage (V) and current (I) are known?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 3.9, p. 22
Questions.Explanation: Ohm's Law states V = I * R, which transposes to R = V / I.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: An amateur signal spectrogram shows power concentrated 2.7 kHz ABOVE the carrier frequency. What mode is being used?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 11.6, p. 157 / Sample Exam Q13
Questions.Explanation: Upper Sideband (USB) places the voice intelligence in the spectrum segment higher than (above) the suppressed carrier frequency.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What circuit configuration converts AC into pulsing DC using four diodes?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 10.6.3, p. 132
Questions.Explanation: A bridge rectifier uses 4 diodes in a bridge arrangement to conduct current during both positive and negative AC half-cycles.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What transformer turns ratio (Np : Ns) is needed to step down 230V mains voltage to 11.5V?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 10.5.2, p. 128
Questions.Explanation: Turns ratio Np/Ns = Vp/Vs = 230 / 11.5 = 20:1.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the purpose of a Zener diode in power supply circuits?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 10.1, p. 121
Questions.Explanation: Zener diodes operate in reverse breakdown mode to maintain a constant reference voltage for regulation.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: In a Direct Sampling SDR receiver, what primary component digitizes incoming RF signals directly from the antenna?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.6.1, p. 199
Questions.Explanation: Direct sampling SDRs use a high-speed ADC to digitize the raw RF spectrum straight from the antenna input.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: According to Carson's Rule, what is the total bandwidth required for an FM voice transmission?
Options: Equal to the peak frequency deviation Δf
Twice the sum of peak frequency deviation and highest modulating audio frequency: BW = 2*(Δf + fmax)
Twice the highest modulating audio frequency
Questions.Correct answer: Twice the sum of peak frequency deviation and highest modulating audio frequency: BW = 2*(Δf + fmax)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 11.4.2, p. 155 / Sample Exam Q20
Questions.Explanation: Carson's Rule states FM bandwidth BW ≈ 2 * (Peak Deviation + Max Audio Frequency).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the typical bandwidth occupied by an FT8 digital mode transmission?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 11.10, p. 166
Questions.Explanation: FT8 uses 8-frequency shift keying (8-FSK) with a ultra-narrow tone spacing, occupying approximately 50 Hz bandwidth.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: In a superheterodyne receiver with an IF of 455 kHz tuned to 7,100 kHz (using high-side LO injection at 7,555 kHz), what is the image frequency?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.7.4, p. 203
Questions.Explanation: High-side injection LO = 7100 + 455 = 7555 kHz. Image = LO + IF = 7555 + 455 = 8010 kHz (or Fin + 2*IF = 7100 + 910 = 8010 kHz).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the front-to-back ratio of a directional Yagi antenna?
Options: The ratio of boom length to element diameter
The ratio of power radiated in the main forward lobe to power radiated in the opposite reverse direction (expressed in dB)
The ratio of input impedance to output impedance
The ratio of total height to ground reflection
Questions.Correct answer: The ratio of power radiated in the main forward lobe to power radiated in the opposite reverse direction (expressed in dB)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 15.16, p. 248
Questions.Explanation: Front-to-back ratio compares radiation intensity in the desired forward direction versus 180° directly behind it.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Calculate ERP in dBW for a 100W transmitter (20 dBW) connected to a line with 1 dB loss and an antenna with 5 dBd gain.
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 15.20.1, p. 251
Questions.Explanation: ERP (dBW) = Transmit power (20 dBW) - Line loss (1 dB) + Antenna gain (5 dBd) = 24 dBW (250 Watts).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What parasitic element in a 3-element Yagi antenna is slightly LONGER than the driven element?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 15.14, p. 243
Questions.Explanation: In a Yagi-Uda antenna, the reflector is ~5% longer than the driven element, while the director is ~5% shorter.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What characteristic impedance is standard for coaxial cables used in modern amateur radio antenna feeders?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 14.6, p. 211 / Sample Exam Q21
Questions.Explanation: Standard amateur radio coaxial cables (RG-58, RG-213) have a characteristic impedance (Z0) of 50 ohms.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the line-of-sight radio horizon distance compared to the visual optical horizon?
Options: Radio horizon is identical to optical horizon
Radio horizon extends to 1,000 km for all frequencies
Radio horizon is approximately 15% further than optical horizon due to atmospheric refraction
Radio horizon is twice as short as optical horizon
Questions.Correct answer: Radio horizon is approximately 15% further than optical horizon due to atmospheric refraction
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.4, p. 261
Questions.Explanation: Normal atmospheric density gradients bend (refract) radio waves downward slightly, extending the radio horizon ~15% beyond optical sight.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Why is daytime long-distance skywave communication generally impossible on the 160m (1.8 MHz) band?
Options: The F-layer disappears completely during the day
The ionospheric D-layer absorbs 160m signals heavily during daylight
Questions.Correct answer: The ionospheric D-layer absorbs 160m signals heavily during daylight
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.5, p. 262 & Ch 16.6, p. 263 / Sample Exam Q25
Questions.Explanation: Sunlight ionizes the low-altitude D-layer during the day, which heavily absorbs low-frequency (LF/MF/160m) radio waves.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What effect do geomagnetic storms triggered by Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) have on HF skywave paths crossing polar regions?
Options: Severe ionospheric disturbances causing auroral absorption and HF blackout
Stabilization of all MUFs above 50 MHz
Questions.Correct answer: Severe ionospheric disturbances causing auroral absorption and HF blackout
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.2.4, p. 257
Questions.Explanation: Solar flares and CMEs disturb Earth's magnetic field, causing radio blackouts and polar path absorption.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Why does a lower radiation angle (takeoff angle) from an HF antenna increase communication distance?
Options: Lower takeoff angles bypass the ionosphere completely
Lower takeoff angles eliminate multipath fading
Lower takeoff angles hit the ionosphere further out, producing longer single-hop skip distances
Lower takeoff angles increase transmitter ERP by 6 dB
Questions.Correct answer: Lower takeoff angles hit the ionosphere further out, producing longer single-hop skip distances
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.7, p. 265
Questions.Explanation: Low takeoff angles strike the ionospheric refracting layer closer to the horizon, expanding the ground distance per hop.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: How should an ammeter be connected to measure current flowing through a circuit branch?
Options: In parallel across the power source
In series within the circuit branch
Questions.Correct answer: In series within the circuit branch
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 17.1.2, p. 273
Questions.Explanation: Ammeters have very low internal resistance and must be inserted in series so the branch current flows through the meter.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What internal resistance characteristics are ideal for a voltmeter and an ammeter?
Options: Voltmeter: extremely high resistance; Ammeter: extremely low resistance
Voltmeter: zero resistance; Ammeter: infinite resistance
Questions.Correct answer: Voltmeter: extremely high resistance; Ammeter: extremely low resistance
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 17.1, p. 272
Questions.Explanation: High voltmeter resistance prevents loading parallel circuits; low ammeter resistance prevents voltage drops in series circuits.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: How is the call sign 'NK6GR' spoken correctly using the ITU Phonetic Alphabet?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 23.1, p. 334 / Sample Exam Q31
Questions.Explanation: The ITU phonetic standard is N=November, K=Kilo, 6=Six, G=Golf, R=Romeo.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What operational abbreviation stands for 'Please' in radiotelegraphy?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.3, p. 349
Questions.Explanation: PSE = Please.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What does the Q-code query 'QRZ?' mean?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.1, p. 346 / Sample Exam Q33
Questions.Explanation: QRZ? = Who is calling me?

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What Q-code means 'Shall I stop transmitting?' or 'I am stopping transmission'?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.1, p. 346
Questions.Explanation: QRT = Stop transmission / Station shutting down.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.3 International Distress Signs, Emergency Traffic and Natural Disaster Communications
Questions.Question: What is the designated Irish Emergency Communications Centre of Activity frequency on the 20m band?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.5, p. 344 & Ch 27.3, p. 351
Questions.Explanation: The 20m Irish emergency frequency is 14.300 MHz.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.3 International Distress Signs, Emergency Traffic and Natural Disaster Communications
Questions.Question: What action should you take if you hear a distress call (MAYDAY or SOS) on the radio?
Options: Transmitting a CQ call to inform other stations
Increase power to block the frequency
Stop transmitting immediately, listen carefully, record details, and offer assistance or relay to emergency services (999/112)
Questions.Correct answer: Stop transmitting immediately, listen carefully, record details, and offer assistance or relay to emergency services (999/112)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 27.5, p. 354
Questions.Explanation: Immediately stop transmitting, listen, write down all details, follow Net Control instructions, and call 999/112 if required.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.3 International Distress Signs, Emergency Traffic and Natural Disaster Communications
Questions.Question: What is the primary role of a licensed radio amateur assisting during an emergency?
Options: Providing medical diagnosis over the air
Enforcing local traffic laws on the road
Passing messages accurately by the fastest available reliable means
Taking over command of emergency services
Questions.Correct answer: Passing messages accurately by the fastest available reliable means
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 27.4.6, p. 354
Questions.Explanation: The primary duty of an amateur operator is message delivery; radio is merely one tool among many to get the message through.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: How is the character '/' spoken when identifying a call sign like 'F/EI5ABC' on voice?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.3, p. 322 & Footnote 404
Questions.Explanation: The character '/' is spoken as 'stroke' or 'slash' (e.g., F stroke EI5ABC).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What national call sign prefix identifies an amateur radio station operating from Czechia (Czech Republic)?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 323 / Sample Exam Q38
Questions.Explanation: Czech Republic national prefixes include OK and OL. (Slovakia is OM).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What call sign suffix indicates land-based mobile operation from a vehicle in Ireland?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.7, p. 329
Questions.Explanation: /M is used for land mobile operation from a motor vehicle.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: What is the lowest suppressed carrier dial setting for LSB voice on the 160m (1.8 MHz) band under IARU R1 band plan?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3, p. 341 / Sample Exam Q41
Questions.Explanation: Because LSB audio extends 3 kHz below dial setting, a 1843 kHz dial setting keeps the lower sideband within the 1840 kHz voice segment edge.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: Is maritime mobile (/MM) operation permitted on the 160m (1.8 MHz) band?
Options: No, maritime mobile is not permitted on 160m
Yes, but only in territorial waters
Questions.Correct answer: No, maritime mobile is not permitted on 160m
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.3, p. 343 (Table 25-C)
Questions.Explanation: Maritime mobile operation is NOT permitted on 160m, 60m, 6m, 4m, or 70cm (50-430 MHz sub-segments).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: What maximum transmit power limit (PEP) applies to most primary HF bands (80m, 40m, 20m, 15m, 10m) in Ireland for fixed stations?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.3, p. 343 (Table 25-C)
Questions.Explanation: The standard maximum power limit for full Irish HAREC licensees on primary HF bands is 400W PEP (26 dBW).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: What exclusive frequency range is reserved for propagation beacons on the 2m VHF band?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.4, p. 344 (Table 25-D)
Questions.Explanation: 2m beacon exclusive segment is 144.400 – 144.490 MHz.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: What should an operator do if they accidentally experience interference from another station during a QSO?
Options: Report the station to An Garda Síochána
Assume changing ionospheric conditions or unintentional overlap, remain polite, and politely inquire or move frequency if necessary
Immediately begin shouting abusive language over the air
Questions.Correct answer: Assume changing ionospheric conditions or unintentional overlap, remain polite, and politely inquire or move frequency if necessary
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 28.2, p. 357
Questions.Explanation: Ionospheric propagation changes constantly, causing stations that couldn't hear each other to suddenly overlap. Remain polite and handle calmly.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: When trying to contact a rare DX station during a crowded pile-up, how should an operator behave?
Options: Wait until the DX station finishes an ongoing contact and explicitly asks for replies to CQ
Transmit continuously over other stations to force the DX station to copy you
Send a long un-keyed carrier wave
Transmit your call sign while the DX station is still receiving another station
Questions.Correct answer: Wait until the DX station finishes an ongoing contact and explicitly asks for replies to CQ
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 28.6, p. 359 & Ch 29.3, p. 362 / Sample Exam Q45
Questions.Explanation: Listen carefully and call only when the DX station has finished a contact and signals readiness for new callers.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: Why is self-discipline essential for the survival of amateur radio spectrum privileges?
Options: Because self-discipline allows amateurs to avoid paying electricity bills
Because regulators grant extensive frequency access based on the amateur community's proven track record of self-policing and compliance
Because ITU replaces licenses with commercial permits if discipline fails
Questions.Correct answer: Because regulators grant extensive frequency access based on the amateur community's proven track record of self-policing and compliance
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 28.4, p. 357
Questions.Explanation: Spectrum authorities allocate valuable spectrum to amateurs because the community demonstrates responsible self-discipline.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What does an S-meter reading of '59+20 dB' mean?
Options: Receiver gain is set to 20 dB
Readability 5 (perfect), Signal Strength S9 plus 20 decibels above S9
Questions.Correct answer: Readability 5 (perfect), Signal Strength S9 plus 20 decibels above S9
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.5, p. 369
Questions.Explanation: Signal reports above S9 are given in decibels over S9 (e.g. 59 plus 20 dB over 9).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: An RS signal report of '35' received during a voice contact means:
Options: Signal is readable with considerable difficulty, and strength 5 on the S-meter
Perfectly readable signal, 3 on the S-meter
Questions.Correct answer: Signal is readable with considerable difficulty, and strength 5 on the S-meter
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.5, p. 368 (Table 29-A) / Sample Exam Q48
Questions.Explanation: Readability R3 = Readable with considerable difficulty; Strength S5 = Fairly good signal.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What does 'Roger' mean when spoken during a voice QSO?
Options: Yes, I agree with your political opinion
I have received and understood your last transmission completely
Questions.Correct answer: I have received and understood your last transmission completely
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.3, p. 349 (Footnote 438)
Questions.Explanation: 'Roger' (derived from R = Received) means 'all received correctly'. It does not mean 'yes'.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What prosign or phrase is used on voice to hand over transmission back to the other station?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.1, p. 360
Questions.Explanation: 'Over' indicates invitation for the other station to transmit. ('Out' indicates end of contact).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What is duplex / repeater operation?
Options: Using Morse code and voice at the same time
Transmitting on one frequency and receiving on a different frequency through a repeater station
Transmitting on the same frequency without a repeater
Questions.Correct answer: Transmitting on one frequency and receiving on a different frequency through a repeater station
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.10, p. 331 & Ch 29.1, p. 360
Questions.Explanation: Repeater / split operation uses separate transmit and receive frequencies (duplex offset).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What is the official ITU emission designator for RTTY / digital machine-decoded data using FSK?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 20.6, p. 317
Questions.Explanation: F1B = Frequency shift keying, single channel automatic telegraphy (RTTY/FT8).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What UN specialized agency governs global international telecommunications and spectrum allocations?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 20.1, p. 314
Questions.Explanation: The ITU is the United Nations specialized agency for information and communication technologies.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: Can an Irish HAREC certificate be used to apply for a permanent amateur licence when taking up residence in another CEPT country?
Options: Only after living in the host country for 5 years
Only if you hold a Class 1 Morse license
No, you must re-take the host country's exam in their native language
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.1, p. 320
Questions.Explanation: T/R 61-02 allows holders moving permanently to a participating CEPT nation to obtain a local equivalent license without re-examination.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What call sign prefix is used when visiting Portugal under CEPT T/R 61-01?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 323 (Table 21-A)
Questions.Explanation: Portugal's prefix is CT; visitor format is CT/EI5ABC.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What distinguishes an Irish CEPT Class 1 licence from a CEPT Class 2 licence?
Options: Class 1 requires demonstrated Morse code proficiency (5 WPM), whereas Class 2 does not
Class 1 is valid for 10 years while Class 2 is valid for 1 year
Class 1 allows 400W power while Class 2 allows only 10W
Class 1 includes satellite privileges while Class 2 does not
Questions.Correct answer: Class 1 requires demonstrated Morse code proficiency (5 WPM), whereas Class 2 does not
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.3, p. 328
Questions.Explanation: Both Class 1 and Class 2 grant full HAREC spectrum privileges under CEPT; Class 1 is issued upon proof of Morse code proficiency.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.10 Irish Laws, Regulations, and Licence Conditions
Questions.Question: Under ComReg rules, how often must an Irish amateur station licensee confirm their station particulars (e.g. address and contact details)?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.4, p. 328 / Sample Exam Q60
Questions.Explanation: Irish licenses remain valid indefinitely provided the licensee confirms their details with ComReg every 5 years.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.10 Irish Laws, Regulations, and Licence Conditions
Questions.Question: Are CQ calls that receive no answer required to be logged in the station logbook under ComReg 09/45 Revision R6?
Options: Yes, every single CQ call must be logged
No, unanswered CQ calls are no longer required to be logged under R6
Yes, but only on HF bands
Questions.Correct answer: No, unanswered CQ calls are no longer required to be logged under R6
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.9, p. 331 (Footnote 406)
Questions.Explanation: Under ComReg 09/45 Revision R6, the former requirement to log unanswered CQ calls was officially removed.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.10 Irish Laws, Regulations, and Licence Conditions
Questions.Question: What is the statutory fee refund policy if an amateur licence is cancelled or revoked by ComReg?
Options: Licence fees will not be refunded
Questions.Correct answer: Licence fees will not be refunded
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.4, p. 328
Questions.Explanation: ComReg regulations state licence fees are non-refundable in the event of cancellation or revocation.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the minimum recommended height above standing level for active antenna elements to avoid human contact hazards?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.8.3, p. 304
Questions.Explanation: Antenna elements should be at least 2.4 m above any surface where people stand to avoid touch and burn hazards.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What tool must be used to ensure high-voltage smoothing capacitors in a power supply are fully discharged before touching internal components?
Options: A multimeter on the 10A current scale
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.4.5, p. 298
Questions.Explanation: Bleeder resistors can fail; a shorting stick must be used to guarantee smoothing capacitors are discharged before servicing.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What electrical current level flowing through the human chest cavity is considered potentially fatal by causing ventricular fibrillation?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.3, p. 293
Questions.Explanation: Currents as small as 50 mA across the heart can trigger fatal ventricular fibrillation. Current kills, not just voltage.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: How far away from overhead power lines should an antenna mast or tower be located?
Options: At least twice its own height
Questions.Correct answer: At least twice its own height
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.6.1, p. 299
Questions.Explanation: To prevent catastrophic contact if the mast or tower falls, it must be positioned at least twice its height away from power lines.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Why are the ends of a half-wave dipole antenna particularly dangerous regarding RF contact?
Options: RF current is highest at the ends of a half-wave dipole
The magnetic field is strongest at the ends
RF voltage is highest at the ends of a half-wave dipole
The ends carry DC high voltage from the transmitter
Questions.Correct answer: RF voltage is highest at the ends of a half-wave dipole
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.3.2, p. 294 & Ch 15.7.1, p. 229
Questions.Explanation: A resonant half-wave dipole exhibits maximum RF voltage at its ends, presenting an extreme RF burn and arc hazard.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is 'desensitisation' in a radio receiver?
Options: The thermal noise generated in an un-tuned antenna
The loss of sensitivity due to low battery voltage
A reduction in receiver gain caused by a strong nearby off-frequency signal overloading the front end
The audio distortion occurring during SSB reception
Questions.Correct answer: A reduction in receiver gain caused by a strong nearby off-frequency signal overloading the front end
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.7.7, p. 205
Questions.Explanation: Desensitisation (blocking) occurs when a very strong off-frequency signal drives receiver AGC or RF stages into gain reduction.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Where does intermodulation distortion (IMD) primarily originate in a receiver?
Options: In non-linear stages such as mixers or overdriven RF amplifiers when two strong signals mix
In the DC power supply bridge rectifier
In the audio speaker voice coil
Questions.Correct answer: In non-linear stages such as mixers or overdriven RF amplifiers when two strong signals mix
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.7.8, p. 205 & Ch 18.2, p. 288
Questions.Explanation: Intermodulation occurs when two or more strong out-of-band signals mix in non-linear receiver stages (RF amp/mixer) to produce phantom signals.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What component can be inserted into an audio lead to eliminate RF rectification in an external amplifier?
Options: A ferrite choke or small bypass capacitor
Questions.Correct answer: A ferrite choke or small bypass capacitor
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 18.1.5, p. 286
Questions.Explanation: Ferrite chokes or small high-frequency ceramic capacitors bypass RF signals to ground before they reach non-linear semiconductor junctions.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What type of interference is caused when strong RF fields cause metal joints or corrosion near an antenna to act as rectifying diodes?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 18.1.4, p. 284
Questions.Explanation: Corroded metal structures in strong RF fields act as non-linear diodes, re-radiating intermodulation products across spectrum bands.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: What is the velocity of electromagnetic radio waves in a vacuum?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 7.1, p. 70
Questions.Explanation: Radio waves propagate at the speed of light c ≈ 3 x 10^8 m/s (300,000 km/s).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: An amateur signal spectrogram shows power concentrated 2.7 kHz ABOVE the carrier frequency. What mode is being used?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 11.6, p. 157 / Sample Exam Q13
Questions.Explanation: Upper Sideband (USB) places the voice intelligence in the spectrum segment higher than (above) the suppressed carrier frequency.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: According to Nyquist's sampling theorem, what is the minimum sampling rate required to digitize an analog signal with bandwidth B?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 6.3.4, p. 61
Questions.Explanation: The Nyquist rate states that sampling frequency must be at least twice the highest frequency bandwidth of the analog signal.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: What formula expresses Ohm's law to calculate resistance when voltage (V) and current (I) are known?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 3.9, p. 22
Questions.Explanation: Ohm's Law states V = I * R, which transposes to R = V / I.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the total equivalent resistance of two resistors, 30 ohms and 60 ohms, connected in parallel?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 4.2.5, p. 33

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What circuit configuration converts AC into pulsing DC using four diodes?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 10.6.3, p. 132
Questions.Explanation: A bridge rectifier uses 4 diodes in a bridge arrangement to conduct current during both positive and negative AC half-cycles.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What are the main structural electrodes inside a thermionic triode vacuum tube?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 10.3.1, p. 124
Questions.Explanation: A triode contains a heated cathode emitting electrons, a control grid regulating flow, and an anode collecting electrons.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What detector is specifically used in receivers to demodulate SSB and CW signals?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.3.7, p. 195
Questions.Explanation: SSB and CW lack a transmitted carrier; a product detector mixes the incoming IF signal with a local BFO carrier to recover audio.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the typical bandwidth occupied by an FT8 digital mode transmission?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 11.10, p. 166
Questions.Explanation: FT8 uses 8-frequency shift keying (8-FSK) with a ultra-narrow tone spacing, occupying approximately 50 Hz bandwidth.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What device allows an HF transceiver to operate on VHF or UHF bands by shifting transmit and receive frequencies?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 12.11, p. 186
Questions.Explanation: A transverter converts transmit/receive frequencies between an HF IF band (e.g. 28 MHz) and VHF/UHF bands (e.g. 144 MHz).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: How does Single Sideband (SSB) bandwidth compare to standard Amplitude Modulation (AM)?
Options: SSB occupies twice the bandwidth of AM
SSB bandwidth depends on antenna height
SSB occupies approximately half the bandwidth of AM
SSB occupies identical bandwidth to FM
Questions.Correct answer: SSB occupies approximately half the bandwidth of AM
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 11.6, p. 157 / Sample Exam Q17
Questions.Explanation: SSB suppresses the carrier and one sideband, occupying ~2.4 kHz compared to AM's ~6 kHz (half the bandwidth).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What zone immediately surrounds an active transmitting antenna where non-radiating reactive fields dominate?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 15.2, p. 225
Questions.Explanation: The reactive near field immediately surrounds the antenna wire, where reactive E and H fields store energy without radiating.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What characteristic impedance is standard for coaxial cables used in modern amateur radio antenna feeders?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 14.6, p. 211 / Sample Exam Q21
Questions.Explanation: Standard amateur radio coaxial cables (RG-58, RG-213) have a characteristic impedance (Z0) of 50 ohms.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: JANUARY 2026 ERRATA: How does a centre-fed half-wave antenna behave when operated on odd vs even harmonics of its fundamental frequency?
Options: It cannot be operated on any harmonic frequency
Its impedance is identical on both odd and even harmonics
Its feed point impedance is much easier to match on odd harmonics (e.g. 15m for a 40m dipole) than even harmonics (e.g. 20m) where impedance is extremely high
Even harmonics match easily while odd harmonics cannot be matched
Questions.Correct answer: Its feed point impedance is much easier to match on odd harmonics (e.g. 15m for a 40m dipole) than even harmonics (e.g. 20m) where impedance is extremely high
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Errata Jan 2026, p. 229 / Footnote 290
Questions.Explanation: Per the Jan 2026 Errata: A centre-fed half-wave dipole has low, easy-to-match feedpoint impedance on odd harmonics (like 15m), but very high impedance on even harmonics (like 20m).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: JANUARY 2026 ERRATA: Where should an SWR meter be positioned in a station setup for equipment protection?
Options: Between the microphone and transceiver input
Directly at the antenna feed point outdoors
Immediately after an amplifier (if used) or transceiver, and BEFORE any final low-pass filters
After the low-pass filter and after the antenna tuner
Questions.Correct answer: Immediately after an amplifier (if used) or transceiver, and BEFORE any final low-pass filters
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Errata Jan 2026, p. 276
Questions.Explanation: Per the Jan 2026 Errata: To protect equipment, the SWR meter must be placed immediately after the transceiver/amplifier and BEFORE any final low-pass filters.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What propagation mechanism temperature inversion layer in the lower atmosphere supports long-distance 2m and 70cm VHF/UHF contacts?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.8.4, p. 267
Questions.Explanation: Tropospheric ducting occurs when warm dry air overlies cool moist air, trapping VHF/UHF waves like a waveguide along weather fronts.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the Lowest Usable Frequency (LUF)?
Options: The lowest frequency that provides sufficient signal strength to overcome D-layer absorption and noise on a given path
The frequency of the lowest band allocated to amateurs (160m)
The minimum frequency a transceiver VFO can tune
Questions.Correct answer: The lowest frequency that provides sufficient signal strength to overcome D-layer absorption and noise on a given path
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.10.3, p. 271
Questions.Explanation: LUF is the lower frequency limit for an HF circuit below which D-layer absorption makes the signal unreadable.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What factor is LEAST likely to affect the single-hop skywave skip distance of an HF signal?
Options: Mode of transmission (e.g. SSB vs CW)
Questions.Correct answer: Mode of transmission (e.g. SSB vs CW)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.7, p. 265 / Sample Exam Q26
Questions.Explanation: Skip distance depends on frequency, takeoff angle, and ionospheric layer height; the modulation mode used does not alter radio wave refraction.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Two stations 4 km apart separated by a hill communicate on 160m. What propagation mode is being used?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.5.1, p. 262 / Sample Exam Q27
Questions.Explanation: Ground waves travel along the contour of the Earth, diffracting over hills to provide local daytime MF/160m coverage.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What parameter does an SWR bridge measure to determine standing wave ratio on a feedline?
Options: Forward voltage and reflected voltage on the transmission line
Questions.Correct answer: Forward voltage and reflected voltage on the transmission line
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 17.2, p. 274
Questions.Explanation: An SWR bridge uses directional couplers/diodes to sample forward power/voltage and reflected power/voltage.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What device measures relative RF electric field strength in the vicinity of an antenna or station layout?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 17.8, p. 279
Questions.Explanation: A field strength meter uses a short pickup antenna and diode detector to measure relative local RF field intensity.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: According to ICAO/ITU phonetic pronunciation guidelines, how should the number '9' be spoken?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 23.1, p. 335 (Table 23-B)
Questions.Explanation: The official radiotelephony pronunciation for the digit 9 is 'NIN-er'.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What Q-code asks for receipt confirmation of a transmission or contact card?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.1, p. 346
Questions.Explanation: QSL? = Can you acknowledge receipt? QSL = Confirmation of contact/card.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What Q-code means 'Shall I decrease transmit power?'
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.1, p. 346
Questions.Explanation: QRP? = Shall I decrease power? QRP = Lower power operation.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What does the Q-code query 'QRZ?' mean?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.1, p. 346 / Sample Exam Q33
Questions.Explanation: QRZ? = Who is calling me?

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.3 International Distress Signs, Emergency Traffic and Natural Disaster Communications
Questions.Question: What is the primary role of a licensed radio amateur assisting during an emergency?
Options: Taking over command of emergency services
Providing medical diagnosis over the air
Passing messages accurately by the fastest available reliable means
Enforcing local traffic laws on the road
Questions.Correct answer: Passing messages accurately by the fastest available reliable means
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 27.4.6, p. 354
Questions.Explanation: The primary duty of an amateur operator is message delivery; radio is merely one tool among many to get the message through.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.3 International Distress Signs, Emergency Traffic and Natural Disaster Communications
Questions.Question: What is the designated Irish Emergency Communications Centre of Activity frequency on the 20m band?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.5, p. 344 & Ch 27.3, p. 351
Questions.Explanation: The 20m Irish emergency frequency is 14.300 MHz.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.3 International Distress Signs, Emergency Traffic and Natural Disaster Communications
Questions.Question: What bandwidth allowance surrounds the emergency centres of activity (e.g. 3.660, 7.115, 14.300 MHz)?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.5, p. 344
Questions.Explanation: Emergency centres of activity cover a band segment of +/- 20 kHz around the nominal center frequency.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What national call sign prefix identifies an amateur radio station operating from Czechia (Czech Republic)?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 323 / Sample Exam Q38
Questions.Explanation: Czech Republic national prefixes include OK and OL. (Slovakia is OM).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What national prefix identifies amateur stations in Germany?
Options: DL (or DA, DB, DF, DG, DH, DK, DM, DO)
Questions.Correct answer: DL (or DA, DB, DF, DG, DH, DK, DM, DO)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 323 (Table 21-A)
Questions.Explanation: Germany's national prefixes include DL, DK, DB, DA, etc. (PA = Netherlands, ON = Belgium, OE = Austria).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What national prefix identifies amateur radio stations in Northern Ireland?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 324 (Table 21-B)
Questions.Explanation: UK regional prefixes: G/M = England, GI/MI = Northern Ireland, GM/MM = Scotland, GW/MW = Wales.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: What maximum power limit applies to land mobile (/M) operation on the 4m (70 MHz) band in Ireland?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.7, p. 329 / Sample Exam Q59
Questions.Explanation: Land mobile operation on 70 MHz (4m) is limited to 25W PEP.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: If ComReg regulations and IARU Band Plans conflict, which document takes legal precedence?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.1, p. 338
Questions.Explanation: ComReg statutory license guidelines always take legal precedence over voluntary IARU band plans.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: Is maritime mobile (/MM) operation permitted on the 160m (1.8 MHz) band?
Options: Yes, but only in territorial waters
No, maritime mobile is not permitted on 160m
Questions.Correct answer: No, maritime mobile is not permitted on 160m
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.3, p. 343 (Table 25-C)
Questions.Explanation: Maritime mobile operation is NOT permitted on 160m, 60m, 6m, 4m, or 70cm (50-430 MHz sub-segments).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: What maximum transmit power limit (PEP) applies to most primary HF bands (80m, 40m, 20m, 15m, 10m) in Ireland for fixed stations?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.3, p. 343 (Table 25-C)
Questions.Explanation: The standard maximum power limit for full Irish HAREC licensees on primary HF bands is 400W PEP (26 dBW).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: How should constructive feedback or correction be offered to a newcomer who makes an operating mistake?
Options: By reporting them immediately for license revocation
Politely and privately or off-air, offering helpful guidance without public embarrassment
By jamming their transmissions until they stop
By reprimanding them loudly over the air in front of everyone
Questions.Correct answer: Politely and privately or off-air, offering helpful guidance without public embarrassment
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 28.1, p. 357
Questions.Explanation: Help newcomers learn by offering polite, friendly advice off-air or constructively without causing public humiliation.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: Why is self-discipline essential for the survival of amateur radio spectrum privileges?
Options: Because regulators grant extensive frequency access based on the amateur community's proven track record of self-policing and compliance
Because ITU replaces licenses with commercial permits if discipline fails
Because self-discipline allows amateurs to avoid paying electricity bills
Questions.Correct answer: Because regulators grant extensive frequency access based on the amateur community's proven track record of self-policing and compliance
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 28.4, p. 357
Questions.Explanation: Spectrum authorities allocate valuable spectrum to amateurs because the community demonstrates responsible self-discipline.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: What is the golden rule of amateur radio operation emphasized across all operating guides?
Options: Listen, listen, and listen again before transmitting
Always transmit at maximum allowed power
Questions.Correct answer: Listen, listen, and listen again before transmitting
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 28.6, p. 359
Questions.Explanation: Listening before transmitting prevents breaking into existing contacts or interfering with ongoing emergency/DX traffic.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What prosign or phrase is used on voice to hand over transmission back to the other station?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.1, p. 360
Questions.Explanation: 'Over' indicates invitation for the other station to transmit. ('Out' indicates end of contact).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What does 'Roger' mean when spoken during a voice QSO?
Options: Yes, I agree with your political opinion
I have received and understood your last transmission completely
Questions.Correct answer: I have received and understood your last transmission completely
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.3, p. 349 (Footnote 438)
Questions.Explanation: 'Roger' (derived from R = Received) means 'all received correctly'. It does not mean 'yes'.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What does 'RST 579' mean on a CW contact?
Options: Readability 5 (perfect), Signal Strength 7 (moderately strong), Tone 9 (perfect tone)
Questions.Correct answer: Readability 5 (perfect), Signal Strength 7 (moderately strong), Tone 9 (perfect tone)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.5, p. 367
Questions.Explanation: R=5 (Perfectly readable), S=7 (Moderately strong signal), T=9 (Perfect clear tone).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: An RS signal report of '35' received during a voice contact means:
Options: Perfectly readable signal, 3 on the S-meter
Signal is readable with considerable difficulty, and strength 5 on the S-meter
Questions.Correct answer: Signal is readable with considerable difficulty, and strength 5 on the S-meter
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.5, p. 368 (Table 29-A) / Sample Exam Q48
Questions.Explanation: Readability R3 = Readable with considerable difficulty; Strength S5 = Fairly good signal.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What does the prosign '<AR>' mean at the end of an initial call in Morse code?
Options: End of message / end of call
Questions.Correct answer: End of message / end of call
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.3.2, p. 363 (Footnote 456)
Questions.Explanation: <AR> (sent as a concatenated prosign .-.-.) denotes end of message / call.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What is the official ITU emission designator for full double-sideband AM voice?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 20.6, p. 317
Questions.Explanation: A3E = Double sideband AM voice telephony.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: How does the ITU define the 'Amateur Service'?
Options: A radiocommunication service for self-training, intercommunication, and technical investigations carried out solely with a personal aim and without pecuniary interest
A commercial broadcasting service for profit
Questions.Correct answer: A radiocommunication service for self-training, intercommunication, and technical investigations carried out solely with a personal aim and without pecuniary interest
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 20.3, p. 315
Questions.Explanation: ITU Article 1.56 defines Amateur Service as non-commercial, self-training, and technical investigation without financial gain.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What call sign prefix should an Irish operator use while visiting the USA under CEPT T/R 61-01?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 324 (Table 21-C)
Questions.Explanation: USA CEPT visitor prefix is W/ or K/ or N/ (e.g. W/EI5ABC or W2/EI5ABC).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What call sign prefix should an Irish operator use while visiting Spain under CEPT T/R 61-01?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 323 (Table 21-A)
Questions.Explanation: Spain's national prefix is EA; the call sign format is EA/EI5ABC.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What CEPT Recommendation defines the Harmonised Amateur Radio Examination Certificate (HAREC) standard?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.1, p. 320
Questions.Explanation: T/R 61-02 defines the standard HAREC examination syllabus accepted across CEPT member nations.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.10 Irish Laws, Regulations, and Licence Conditions
Questions.Question: If a licensed radio amateur constructs their own transmitter (DIY) without a CE mark, who assumes legal responsibility for safety and non-interference?
Options: The manufacturer of the soldering iron
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.12, p. 332
Questions.Explanation: Radio amateurs are legally permitted to build un-marked homebrew transmitters, but assume 100% personal responsibility for EMC, spurious limits, and safety.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.10 Irish Laws, Regulations, and Licence Conditions
Questions.Question: Under what circumstances can ComReg suspend or revoke an amateur station licence?
Options: In the event of serious or repeated non-compliance with licence conditions
If the licensee fails to make 100 contacts per year
If the licensee changes their antenna type
If the licensee operates on 20m during nighttime
Questions.Correct answer: In the event of serious or repeated non-compliance with licence conditions
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.4, p. 328
Questions.Explanation: ComReg may suspend or revoke a licence for serious or repeated non-compliance with statutory regulations or licence terms.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.10 Irish Laws, Regulations, and Licence Conditions
Questions.Question: What clock time format must be used for recording transmission times in an Irish station logbook?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.9, p. 331
Questions.Explanation: Logbook entries must be recorded in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
