Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: When adjusting live high-voltage valve equipment, what safety rule should always be observed?
Options: Wear rubber gloves on both hands
Touch the chassis with both thumbs
Keep one hand behind your back
Questions.Correct answer: Keep one hand behind your back
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.3, p. 293 & Ch 19.4.6, p. 299
Questions.Explanation: Keeping one hand behind your back prevents forming a current path across the chest cavity between two hands.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Which earthing system is standardly used in Irish mains power installations?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.4.2, p. 296
Questions.Explanation: Ireland uses the TN-C-S (Terra Neutral Combined and Separated) earthing system. Operators must ensure all earths are properly bonded.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the primary biological hazard associated with exposure to high-intensity RF electromagnetic fields?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.8.3, p. 303
Questions.Explanation: RF EMF is non-ionising radiation; its principal adverse biological effect is the thermal heating of human tissue.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the first action you should take if you suspect a person is receiving an electric shock?
Options: Shut off the mains power before touching them
Immediately pull them away with your bare hands
Questions.Correct answer: Shut off the mains power before touching them
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.3.1, p. 293
Questions.Explanation: Never touch a victim of electric shock until the power source is shut off, to avoid becoming part of the circuit yourself.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What electrical current level flowing through the human chest cavity is considered potentially fatal by causing ventricular fibrillation?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.3, p. 293
Questions.Explanation: Currents as small as 50 mA across the heart can trigger fatal ventricular fibrillation. Current kills, not just voltage.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What type of interference is caused when strong RF fields cause metal joints or corrosion near an antenna to act as rectifying diodes?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 18.1.4, p. 284
Questions.Explanation: Corroded metal structures in strong RF fields act as non-linear diodes, re-radiating intermodulation products across spectrum bands.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is 'desensitisation' in a radio receiver?
Options: The loss of sensitivity due to low battery voltage
The audio distortion occurring during SSB reception
The thermal noise generated in an un-tuned antenna
A reduction in receiver gain caused by a strong nearby off-frequency signal overloading the front end
Questions.Correct answer: A reduction in receiver gain caused by a strong nearby off-frequency signal overloading the front end
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.7.7, p. 205
Questions.Explanation: Desensitisation (blocking) occurs when a very strong off-frequency signal drives receiver AGC or RF stages into gain reduction.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is cross-modulation in a receiver?
Options: The modulation of a desired weak signal by an unwanted strong modulating signal in a non-linear stage
The conversion of AM signals to FM in the detector
The mixing of IF frequencies with the local oscillator
The reflection of signals from ionospheric E-layers
Questions.Correct answer: The modulation of a desired weak signal by an unwanted strong modulating signal in a non-linear stage
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.7.9, p. 205
Questions.Explanation: Cross-modulation occurs when the modulation from an undesired strong signal transfers onto the carrier of a desired weak signal inside a non-linear RF stage.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What component can be inserted into an audio lead to eliminate RF rectification in an external amplifier?
Options: A ferrite choke or small bypass capacitor
Questions.Correct answer: A ferrite choke or small bypass capacitor
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 18.1.5, p. 286
Questions.Explanation: Ferrite chokes or small high-frequency ceramic capacitors bypass RF signals to ground before they reach non-linear semiconductor junctions.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: According to Nyquist's sampling theorem, what is the minimum sampling rate required to digitize an analog signal with bandwidth B?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 6.3.4, p. 61
Questions.Explanation: The Nyquist rate states that sampling frequency must be at least twice the highest frequency bandwidth of the analog signal.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: What mathematical algorithm is used in DSP to convert time-domain digital signals into the frequency domain?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 6.2.1, p. 56 / Sample Exam Q12
Questions.Explanation: The Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) converts amplitude-vs-time digital samples into frequency-domain spectrum data.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: What is a harmonic frequency?
Options: A frequency exactly half the fundamental frequency
A signal 90 degrees out of phase
An unwanted audio noise produced by speakers
A signal whose frequency is an exact integer multiple of the fundamental frequency
Questions.Correct answer: A signal whose frequency is an exact integer multiple of the fundamental frequency
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 5.4, p. 45
Questions.Explanation: A harmonic is an exact integer multiple (2x, 3x, 4x...) of a fundamental signal frequency.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: What is the velocity of electromagnetic radio waves in a vacuum?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 7.1, p. 70
Questions.Explanation: Radio waves propagate at the speed of light c ≈ 3 x 10^8 m/s (300,000 km/s).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What condition defines electrical resonance in a circuit containing inductors and capacitors?
Options: Inductive reactance is double the capacitive reactance
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 8.3.2, p. 98
Questions.Explanation: Resonance occurs at the frequency fr where XL = XC, causing their reactive oppositions to cancel out.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: In amplifier classification, which class provides highest efficiency (up to 75-80%) but operates in non-linear conduction for less than 180 degrees of the cycle?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 10.7.2, p. 135
Questions.Explanation: Class C amplifiers conduct for less than 180° of the input cycle. They are highly efficient but non-linear (suitable for CW/FM).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: If a 4 ohm resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 30 ohm and 60 ohm resistors across a 12V battery, what is the total circuit current?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 4.2.5, p. 33
Questions.Explanation: Parallel pair = 20 ohms. Total Req = 4 + 20 = 24 ohms. Total current I = V / Req = 12 / 24 = 0.5 A.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: In a traditional SSB transmitter block diagram, what stage combines the speech audio with the carrier oscillator signal?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 12.7.1, p. 178 / Sample Exam Q19
Questions.Explanation: The balanced modulator combines AF speech and RF carrier, producing double-sideband suppressed-carrier (DSB-SC) signals.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: JANUARY 2026 ERRATA: What is the correct receiver IF filter bandwidth range specified for FM signals in Table 13-A?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Errata Jan 2026, p. 193
Questions.Explanation: Per the Jan 2026 Errata update to Table 13-A, receiver IF filter bandwidth for FM is 7.5 – 16 kHz (updated from 12.5 kHz).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What dummy load power rating is required when testing a 100W transmitter?
Options: At least 100W continuous rating into a non-inductive 50 ohm load
Questions.Correct answer: At least 100W continuous rating into a non-inductive 50 ohm load
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 17.10, p. 281
Questions.Explanation: A dummy load must be non-inductive 50 ohms and rated to safely dissipate the transmitter's maximum continuous output power as heat.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What circuit silences the receiver audio output when no RF carrier signal is being received on FM?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.3.12, p. 198
Questions.Explanation: Squelch mutes background thermal noise when no signal above a threshold level is present.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What radiation pattern is produced by a horizontal half-wave dipole in free space?
Options: Figure-eight bidirectional pattern perpendicular to the wire
Omnidirectional circular pattern in all directions
Unidirectional single beam pointing off the wire ends
Questions.Correct answer: Figure-eight bidirectional pattern perpendicular to the wire
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 15.7.1, p. 228
Questions.Explanation: A horizontal half-wave dipole radiates a broad figure-eight pattern maximum broadside (perpendicular) to the wire.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What standing wave ratio (SWR) indicates a perfect impedance match between feeder and load?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 14.9.4, p. 219
Questions.Explanation: An SWR of 1:1 indicates zero reflected power and complete impedance matching.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What feedline type exhibits the lowest attenuation loss over long distances at HF?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 14.5, p. 209
Questions.Explanation: Air-dielectric open-wire parallel line has extremely low dielectric loss compared to coaxial cables.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the front-to-back ratio of a directional Yagi antenna?
Options: The ratio of power radiated in the main forward lobe to power radiated in the opposite reverse direction (expressed in dB)
The ratio of boom length to element diameter
The ratio of input impedance to output impedance
The ratio of total height to ground reflection
Questions.Correct answer: The ratio of power radiated in the main forward lobe to power radiated in the opposite reverse direction (expressed in dB)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 15.16, p. 248
Questions.Explanation: Front-to-back ratio compares radiation intensity in the desired forward direction versus 180° directly behind it.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What ionospheric layer exists only during daylight hours and splits into two distinct sub-layers (F1 and F2)?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.3.3, p. 259
Questions.Explanation: During the day, intense solar radiation splits the F-layer into F1 (~200 km) and F2 (~400 km) layers.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What VHF/UHF propagation mode relies on green curtain auroral displays in high latitudes, imparting a distinctive raspy tone to voice signals?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.8.6, p. 267
Questions.Explanation: Ionized auroral curtains reflect VHF signals; rapid electron movement causes severe Doppler distortion, making voice sound raspy.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Why is daytime long-distance skywave communication generally impossible on the 160m (1.8 MHz) band?
Options: The ionospheric D-layer absorbs 160m signals heavily during daylight
The F-layer disappears completely during the day
Questions.Correct answer: The ionospheric D-layer absorbs 160m signals heavily during daylight
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.5, p. 262 & Ch 16.6, p. 263 / Sample Exam Q25
Questions.Explanation: Sunlight ionizes the low-altitude D-layer during the day, which heavily absorbs low-frequency (LF/MF/160m) radio waves.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: How does the 11-year solar sunspot cycle impact HF radio propagation?
Options: Sunspots cause solar eclipses every 11 years
Higher sunspot numbers increase solar UV/X-ray radiation, boosting ionisation and raising the Maximum Usable Frequency (MUF)
Higher sunspot numbers destroy the ionosphere and block all HF
Sunspots only affect VHF frequencies above 144 MHz
Questions.Correct answer: Higher sunspot numbers increase solar UV/X-ray radiation, boosting ionisation and raising the Maximum Usable Frequency (MUF)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.2.2, p. 256
Questions.Explanation: Sunspot peaks increase solar EUV radiation, charging the ionosphere heavily and supporting high HF bands (15m, 12m, 10m).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What measurement instrument directly counts and displays the numerical frequency of an RF signal?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 17.7, p. 279
Questions.Explanation: A digital frequency counter counts signal cycles over a precise time gate to display the frequency in Hz/kHz/MHz.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What instrument measures complex impedance (resistance and reactance) of an antenna across a range of frequencies?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 17.9, p. 280
Questions.Explanation: An antenna analyzer contains an internal RF signal generator and bridge to measure SWR, R, and X across frequency bands.

Questions.Question: How is the digit '5' pronounced in official radiotelephony spelling?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 23.1, p. 335 (Table 23-B)
Questions.Explanation: The official radiotelephony pronunciation for 5 is 'FIFE'.

Questions.Question: What Q-code means 'Is the frequency busy?' when sent with a question mark?

Questions.Question: What operational abbreviation means 'Break in' during an ongoing conversation?

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What Q-code indicates 'I am ready' or 'Are you ready?'
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.1, p. 346
Questions.Explanation: QRV = I am ready / Are you ready?

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.3 International Distress Signs, Emergency Traffic and Natural Disaster Communications
Questions.Question: Why is specialized training (such as AREN training) recommended before participating in emergency nets?

To receive a paid salary from Civil Defence
To ensure operators understand net discipline and operating procedures without impeding emergency traffic
To learn how to repair commercial emergency transmitters

Questions.Question: What is the designated Irish Emergency Communications Centre of Activity frequency on the 20m band?

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What call sign suffix indicates land-based mobile operation from a vehicle in Ireland?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.7, p. 329

Questions.Question: What national prefix identifies amateur stations in New Zealand?

Options: DL (or DA, DB, DF, DG, DH, DK, DM, DO)

Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 323 (Table 21-A)

Questions.Question: What exclusive frequency range is reserved for propagation beacons on the 20m band?

Questions.Question: What maximum transmit power limit (PEP) applies to most primary HF bands (80m, 40m, 20m, 15m, 10m) in Ireland for fixed stations?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.3, p. 343 (Table 25-C)
Questions.Explanation: The standard maximum power limit for full Irish HAREC licensees on primary HF bands is 400W PEP (26 dBW).

Questions.Question: What is the lowest suppressed carrier dial setting for LSB voice on the 160m (1.8 MHz) band under IARU R1 band plan?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3, p. 341 / Sample Exam Q41

Questions.Question: What exclusive frequency range is reserved for propagation beacons on the 2m VHF band?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.4, p. 344 (Table 25-D)
Questions.Explanation: 2m beacon exclusive segment is 144.400 – 144.490 MHz.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: What tone of voice and language is expected during all amateur radio communications?
Options: Polite, civil, non-derogatory, and constructive language at all times
Questions.Correct answer: Polite, civil, non-derogatory, and constructive language at all times
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 28.5, p. 358
Questions.Explanation: Amateur radio is a public, open medium shared by families and international operators; courtesy and politeness are mandatory.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: What is the correct sequence of actions before making a CQ call on an apparently clear frequency?
Options: Call CQ immediately at full power
Listen to check if the frequency is clear; ask 'Is this frequency in use, this is [Callsign]'; listen; then call CQ if clear
Transmit a 10-second carrier test tone then call CQ
Ask 'Is the frequency clear?' and immediately begin calling CQ without waiting
Questions.Correct answer: Listen to check if the frequency is clear; ask 'Is this frequency in use, this is [Callsign]'; listen; then call CQ if clear
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.3.1, p. 362 / Sample Exam Q46
Questions.Explanation: Always listen first, explicitly ask if the frequency is in use giving your call sign, listen for a reply, and proceed only if clear.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: What fundamental principle governs behavior and band usage within the amateur radio community?
Options: ComReg daily monitoring officers on every channel
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 28.4, p. 357
Questions.Explanation: Amateur radio relies on voluntary self-regulation, mutual respect, and self-discipline to ensure fair spectrum sharing.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What three components make up a standard RST signal report exchanged on CW contacts?
Options: Receiver type, SWR ratio, Transmitter power

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What does a Tone report of less than 'T9' indicate on a CW signal report?
Options: That the station is using an electronic keyer
That the operator is sending at high speed
A defect or unwanted hum/ripple in the transmitter signal's tonal quality
Questions.Correct answer: A defect or unwanted hum/ripple in the transmitter signal's tonal quality
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.5, p. 369
Questions.Explanation: Modern clean CW transmitters produce T9 (pure tone). T1-T8 indicates AC ripple, key clicks, or chirp defects.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What traditional greeting abbreviation means 'Best regards' in amateur radio contacts?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.3, p. 349
Questions.Explanation: 73 = Best regards. (88 = Love and kisses).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What does an S-meter reading of '59+20 dB' mean?
Options: Readability 5 (perfect), Signal Strength S9 plus 20 decibels above S9
Receiver gain is set to 20 dB
Questions.Correct answer: Readability 5 (perfect), Signal Strength S9 plus 20 decibels above S9
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.5, p. 369
Questions.Explanation: Signal reports above S9 are given in decibels over S9 (e.g. 59 plus 20 dB over 9).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What is simplex operation?
Options: Stations transmit on one frequency and receive on a different frequency
Both stations transmit and receive on the exact same single frequency (one station speaks at a time)
Questions.Correct answer: Both stations transmit and receive on the exact same single frequency (one station speaks at a time)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.1, p. 360 (Footnote 449)
Questions.Explanation: Simplex operation uses one single frequency for both transmitting and receiving sequentially.

Questions.Question: What is the official ITU emission designator for RTTY / digital machine-decoded data using FSK?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 20.6, p. 317

Questions.Question: What is the official ITU emission designator for Single Sideband (SSB) suppressed carrier voice?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 20.6, p. 317 / Sample Exam Q54

Questions.Question: What call sign prefix should an Irish operator use while visiting the USA under CEPT T/R 61-01?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 324 (Table 21-C)

Questions.Question: What call sign prefix is used when visiting Portugal under CEPT T/R 61-01?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 323 (Table 21-A)

Questions.Question: Under what circumstances can ComReg suspend or revoke an amateur station licence?

In the event of serious or repeated non-compliance with licence conditions
If the licensee changes their antenna type
If the licensee fails to make 100 contacts per year

Questions.Question: Who is legally permitted to operate an Irish amateur radio station?

The licensee, or an unlicensed person operating under the direct personal supervision of the licensee
Only members of the IRTS committee
Anyone holding a commercial broadcast permit

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What tool must be used to ensure high-voltage smoothing capacitors in a power supply are fully discharged before touching internal components?
Options: A multimeter on the 10A current scale
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.4.5, p. 298
Questions.Explanation: Bleeder resistors can fail; a shorting stick must be used to guarantee smoothing capacitors are discharged before servicing.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: Which directive restricts the use of hazardous substances like lead and cadmium in electronic equipment?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.7, p. 300 / Syllabus A.1
Questions.Explanation: The EU Reduction of Hazardous Substances (RoHS) directive restricts toxic materials in electronic products.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What electrical current level flowing through the human chest cavity is considered potentially fatal by causing ventricular fibrillation?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.3, p. 293
Questions.Explanation: Currents as small as 50 mA across the heart can trigger fatal ventricular fibrillation. Current kills, not just voltage.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: When soldering radio circuits, what safety precaution should be taken regarding chemical fumes?
Options: Keep a fire extinguisher in hand
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.7, p. 300
Questions.Explanation: Flux fumes from soldering can cause respiratory irritation and asthma; soldering must occur in well-ventilated spaces.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What type of burn is caused by direct physical contact with an active transmitting antenna?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 19.3.2, p. 294
Questions.Explanation: Direct contact or arcing from energised RF conductors causes painful deep-tissue RF burns.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is 'desensitisation' in a radio receiver?
Options: The thermal noise generated in an un-tuned antenna
A reduction in receiver gain caused by a strong nearby off-frequency signal overloading the front end
The loss of sensitivity due to low battery voltage
The audio distortion occurring during SSB reception
Questions.Correct answer: A reduction in receiver gain caused by a strong nearby off-frequency signal overloading the front end
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.7.7, p. 205
Questions.Explanation: Desensitisation (blocking) occurs when a very strong off-frequency signal drives receiver AGC or RF stages into gain reduction.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the term for a non-susceptible electronic device malfunctioning purely due to strong legitimate local RF emissions exceeding its shielding?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 18.1.3, p. 283
Questions.Explanation: When equipment malfunctions due to strong external RF signals because the device itself lacks adequate internal immunity or shielding, it is called RF breakthrough.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What type of interference is caused when strong RF fields cause metal joints or corrosion near an antenna to act as rectifying diodes?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 18.1.4, p. 284
Questions.Explanation: Corroded metal structures in strong RF fields act as non-linear diodes, re-radiating intermodulation products across spectrum bands.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: How does a band-pass filter behave?
Options: It passes frequencies within a specified range and attenuates frequencies above and below it
It passes all frequencies except one specific notch frequency
Questions.Correct answer: It passes frequencies within a specified range and attenuates frequencies above and below it
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 8.4.2, p. 106 / Sample Exam Q8
Questions.Explanation: A band-pass filter allows signals within a designated frequency band to pass while blocking lower and higher frequencies.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: What is the electric field strength unit of measurement?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 7.6, p. 85
Questions.Explanation: Electric field strength (E-field) is measured in Volts per metre (V/m). Power density is measured in W/m^2.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: What formula expresses Ohm's law to calculate resistance when voltage (V) and current (I) are known?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 3.9, p. 22
Questions.Explanation: Ohm's Law states V = I * R, which transposes to R = V / I.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Subsection: A.3 Electrical, Electromagnetic, and Radio Theory
Questions.Question: What is the unit and dimension symbol for electric charge or battery capacity?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 3.2.1, p. 14
Questions.Explanation: Battery capacity is commonly measured in Ampere-hours (A·h), representing current multiplied by time.

Questions.Question: What is the RMS voltage of a sinusoidal AC signal with a peak voltage (Vpeak) of 10 V?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 5.1.5, p. 42 / Sample Exam Q30

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: In amplifier classification, which class provides highest efficiency (up to 75-80%) but operates in non-linear conduction for less than 180 degrees of the cycle?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 10.7.2, p. 135
Questions.Explanation: Class C amplifiers conduct for less than 180° of the input cycle. They are highly efficient but non-linear (suitable for CW/FM).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: How does a parallel LC tuned circuit behave at its resonant frequency when connected in series with a load?
Options: It acts as a high-impedance rejector (blocks the resonant frequency)
It acts as a low-impedance acceptor (passes the resonant frequency)
It amplifies all signals by 10 dB
Questions.Correct answer: It acts as a high-impedance rejector (blocks the resonant frequency)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 8.4.1, p. 103
Questions.Explanation: A parallel LC circuit exhibits maximum impedance at resonance, acting as a rejector trap when placed in line.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What are the main structural electrodes inside a thermionic triode vacuum tube?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 10.3.1, p. 124
Questions.Explanation: A triode contains a heated cathode emitting electrons, a control grid regulating flow, and an anode collecting electrons.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: JANUARY 2026 ERRATA: What is the correct receiver IF filter bandwidth range specified for FM signals in Table 13-A?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Errata Jan 2026, p. 193
Questions.Explanation: Per the Jan 2026 Errata update to Table 13-A, receiver IF filter bandwidth for FM is 7.5 – 16 kHz (updated from 12.5 kHz).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What parameter describes the ratio between the strongest signal a receiver can handle without overload and the weakest readable signal?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.7.3, p. 203
Questions.Explanation: Dynamic range measures the range of signal strengths a receiver can process simultaneously without distortion or desensitisation.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: In a Direct Sampling SDR receiver, what primary component digitizes incoming RF signals directly from the antenna?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.6.1, p. 199
Questions.Explanation: Direct sampling SDRs use a high-speed ADC to digitize the raw RF spectrum straight from the antenna input.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What does the term 'sensitivity' describe in a radio receiver?
Options: The frequency drift rate per hour
Its ability to reject strong adjacent interfering signals
The total audio output power of the speaker stage
Its ability to successfully receive and decode weak signals
Questions.Correct answer: Its ability to successfully receive and decode weak signals
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 13.7.1, p. 202 / Sample Exam Q18
Questions.Explanation: Sensitivity is the receiver's capability to resolve weak signals above the internal noise floor.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: If a transmission feedline must run close to metallic structures or building walls, which feedline type should be used?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 14.6, p. 211 / Sample Exam Q22
Questions.Explanation: Coaxial cable confines its electromagnetic fields entirely within its outer shielded braid, preventing interference from nearby conductive objects.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the front-to-back ratio of a directional Yagi antenna?

The ratio of total height to ground reflection
The ratio of boom length to element diameter
The ratio of input impedance to output impedance
Questions.Correct answer: The ratio of power radiated in the main forward lobe to power radiated in the opposite reverse direction (expressed in dB)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 15.16, p. 248
Questions.Explanation: Front-to-back ratio compares radiation intensity in the desired forward direction versus 180° directly behind it.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What ratio defines Effective Isotropic Radiated Power (EIRP)?
Options: The transmitter output power minus SWR loss
The DC input power multiplied by efficiency
The total power radiated relative to an ideal isotropic radiator in free space
The power radiated relative to a half-wave dipole
Questions.Correct answer: The total power radiated relative to an ideal isotropic radiator in free space
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 15.20, p. 250
Questions.Explanation: EIRP measures effective focused power relative to an isotropic source (dBi = dBd + 2.15).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What parasitic element in a 3-element Yagi antenna is slightly LONGER than the driven element?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 15.14, p. 243
Questions.Explanation: In a Yagi-Uda antenna, the reflector is ~5% longer than the driven element, while the director is ~5% shorter.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: How does the 11-year solar sunspot cycle impact HF radio propagation?
Options: Higher sunspot numbers destroy the ionosphere and block all HF
Sunspots only affect VHF frequencies above 144 MHz
Sunspots cause solar eclipses every 11 years
Higher sunspot numbers increase solar UV/X-ray radiation, boosting ionisation and raising the Maximum Usable Frequency (MUF)
Questions.Correct answer: Higher sunspot numbers increase solar UV/X-ray radiation, boosting ionisation and raising the Maximum Usable Frequency (MUF)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.2.2, p. 256
Questions.Explanation: Sunspot peaks increase solar EUV radiation, charging the ionosphere heavily and supporting high HF bands (15m, 12m, 10m).

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What effect do geomagnetic storms triggered by Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) have on HF skywave paths crossing polar regions?
Options: Stabilization of all MUFs above 50 MHz
Severe ionospheric disturbances causing auroral absorption and HF blackout
Questions.Correct answer: Severe ionospheric disturbances causing auroral absorption and HF blackout
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.2.4, p. 257
Questions.Explanation: Solar flares and CMEs disturb Earth's magnetic field, causing radio blackouts and polar path absorption.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What propagation mode utilizes the brief ionized trails of disintegrating space debris in the upper atmosphere to bounce VHF signals?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.8.7, p. 267
Questions.Explanation: Meteors burning up in the E-region leave brief ionized trails that reflect 6m and 2m signals for milliseconds to seconds.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What is the Lowest Usable Frequency (LUF)?
Options: The frequency of the lowest band allocated to amateurs (160m)
The lowest frequency that provides sufficient signal strength to overcome D-layer absorption and noise on a given path
The minimum frequency a transceiver VFO can tune
Questions.Correct answer: The lowest frequency that provides sufficient signal strength to overcome D-layer absorption and noise on a given path
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 16.10.3, p. 271
Questions.Explanation: LUF is the lower frequency limit for an HF circuit below which D-layer absorption makes the signal unreadable.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: What measurement instrument directly counts and displays the numerical frequency of an RF signal?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 17.7, p. 279
Questions.Explanation: A digital frequency counter counts signal cycles over a precise time gate to display the frequency in Hz/kHz/MHz.

Questions.Section: Section A: Technical
Questions.Question: When using an oscilloscope to analyze a transmitter RF output, what does the vertical (Y) axis display?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 17.3, p. 276 / Sample Exam Q29
Questions.Explanation: On an oscilloscope display, the vertical Y-axis represents instantaneous signal voltage, while the horizontal X-axis represents time.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What is the correct ITU phonetic codeword for the letter 'Z'?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 23.1, p. 335 (Table 23-A)
Questions.Explanation: Z = Zulu.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What Q-code indicates 'I am ready' or 'Are you ready?'
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.1, p. 346
Questions.Explanation: QRV = I am ready / Are you ready?

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What Q-code means 'Shall I stop transmitting?' or 'I am stopping transmission'?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.1, p. 346
Questions.Explanation: QRT = Stop transmission / Station shutting down.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What CW abbreviation stands for 'End of Work' / 'Closing Station'?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 26.3, p. 349
Questions.Explanation: SK (prosign) = End of work / Final closure of contact.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.3 International Distress Signs, Emergency Traffic and Natural Disaster Communications
Questions.Question: What is the designated Irish Emergency Communications Centre of Activity frequency on the 80m HF band?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.5, p. 344 & Ch 27.3, p. 351 / Sample Exam Q36
Questions.Explanation: The Irish emergency frequencies are: 80m = 3.660 MHz, 40m = 7.115 MHz, 20m = 14.300 MHz.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.3 International Distress Signs, Emergency Traffic and Natural Disaster Communications
Questions.Question: What is the primary role of a licensed radio amateur assisting during an emergency?
Options: Enforcing local traffic laws on the road
Passing messages accurately by the fastest available reliable means
Taking over command of emergency services
Providing medical diagnosis over the air
Questions.Correct answer: Passing messages accurately by the fastest available reliable means
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 27.4.6, p. 354
Questions.Explanation: The primary duty of an amateur operator is message delivery; radio is merely one tool among many to get the message through.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.3 International Distress Signs, Emergency Traffic and Natural Disaster Communications
Questions.Question: Why is specialized training (such as AREN training) recommended before participating in emergency nets?
Options: To learn how to repair commercial emergency transmitters
Because untrained operators are legally prohibited from owning radios
To receive a paid salary from Civil Defence
To ensure operators understand net discipline and operating procedures without impeding emergency traffic
Questions.Correct answer: To ensure operators understand net discipline and operating procedures without impeding emergency traffic
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 27.4, p. 351
Questions.Explanation: Emergency traffic requires strict net discipline and concise procedures so untrained well-meaning operators do not cause confusion.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What national prefix identifies amateur radio stations in Northern Ireland?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 324 (Table 21-B)
Questions.Explanation: UK regional prefixes: G/M = England, GI/MI = Northern Ireland, GM/MM = Scotland, GW/MW = Wales.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: According to ITU Radio Regulations format rules, which of these is a valid amateur call sign structure?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 24.2, p. 336 / Sample Exam Q40
Questions.Explanation: Standard ITU call signs consist of prefix (1-2 chars), a single digit (e.g. 6), and a suffix (1-4 chars ending in a letter). '2E6J' fits this format.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What national prefix identifies amateur stations in Germany?
Options: DL (or DA, DB, DF, DG, DH, DK, DM, DO)
Questions.Correct answer: DL (or DA, DB, DF, DG, DH, DK, DM, DO)
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.4, p. 323 (Table 21-A)
Questions.Explanation: Germany's national prefixes include DL, DK, DB, DA, etc. (PA = Netherlands, ON = Belgium, OE = Austria).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: What is the authorized frequency range for the 70 centimetre UHF band in Ireland?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.3, p. 343 (Table 25-C)
Questions.Explanation: The 70cm band allocation in Ireland is 430.000 MHz to 440.000 MHz.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: What is the power limit on 70cm between 430.000 MHz and 432.000 MHz in Ireland?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.3, p. 343 (Table 25-C)
Questions.Explanation: Between 430–432 MHz power is limited to 50W PEP; above 432 MHz up to 400W PEP is allowed.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: Under the IARU Region 1 Band Plan, what operating mode is preferred in the 3.510–3.570 MHz range on 80m?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.1, p. 342 (Table 25-B) / Sample Exam Q42
Questions.Explanation: 3510–3570 kHz is reserved exclusively for CW telegraphy.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.5 Radio Spectrum Allocation in Ireland and IARU Band Plans
Questions.Question: What is the lowest dial setting for LSB voice on 80m to keep the 2.7 kHz sideband inside the 3.600 MHz band segment boundary?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 25.3.1, p. 342 (Table 25-B)
Questions.Explanation: LSB audio extends 2.7–3 kHz BELOW the dial frequency; setting 3603 kHz keeps the emissions above 3600 kHz.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: Can a licensed radio amateur conduct commercial business or advertise products for sale on the air?
Options: Yes, if paying a 10% tax to ComReg
No, amateur radio must be conducted solely with a personal aim and strictly without pecuniary (financial) interest
Questions.Correct answer: No, amateur radio must be conducted solely with a personal aim and strictly without pecuniary (financial) interest
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 20.3, p. 315 & Ch 29.2.1, p. 361
Questions.Explanation: ITU and ComReg rules strictly prohibit any business, commercial advertising, or pecuniary interest on amateur bands.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: What is the correct sequence of actions before making a CQ call on an apparently clear frequency?
Options: Listen to check if the frequency is clear; ask 'Is this frequency in use, this is [Callsign]'; listen; then call CQ if clear
Ask 'Is the frequency clear?' and immediately begin calling CQ without waiting
Call CQ immediately at full power
Transmit a 10-second carrier test tone then call CQ
Questions.Correct answer: Listen to check if the frequency is clear; ask 'Is this frequency in use, this is [Callsign]'; listen; then call CQ if clear
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.3.1, p. 362 / Sample Exam Q46
Questions.Explanation: Always listen first, explicitly ask if the frequency is in use giving your call sign, listen for a reply, and proceed only if clear.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.6 Social Responsibility of Radio Amateur Operation and the Code of Conduct
Questions.Question: What is the golden rule of amateur radio operation emphasized across all operating guides?
Options: Always transmit at maximum allowed power
Listen, listen, and listen again before transmitting
Questions.Correct answer: Listen, listen, and listen again before transmitting
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 28.6, p. 359
Questions.Explanation: Listening before transmitting prevents breaking into existing contacts or interfering with ongoing emergency/DX traffic.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What is duplex / repeater operation?
Options: Transmitting on one frequency and receiving on a different frequency through a repeater station
Using Morse code and voice at the same time
Transmitting on the same frequency without a repeater
Questions.Correct answer: Transmitting on one frequency and receiving on a different frequency through a repeater station
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.10, p. 331 & Ch 29.1, p. 360
Questions.Explanation: Repeater / split operation uses separate transmit and receive frequencies (duplex offset).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What does the Morse Code message 'CQ CQ CQ DE EI3XYZ <AR>' indicate?
Options: EI3XYZ is making a general call for a contact
EI3XYZ is giving a signal report
Questions.Correct answer: EI3XYZ is making a general call for a contact
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.3.2, p. 363 / Sample Exam Q50
Questions.Explanation: 'CQ ... DE EI3XYZ <AR>' is the standard Morse code general call inviting any station to respond.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What prosign or phrase is used on voice to hand over transmission back to the other station?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.1, p. 360
Questions.Explanation: 'Over' indicates invitation for the other station to transmit. ('Out' indicates end of contact).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: In Morse code QSOs, what abbreviation acknowledges a complete transmission and hands control back?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.4, p. 366
Questions.Explanation: K (or KN for specific station) invites the other station to transmit.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What is the meaning of 'R5' in a readability report?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 29.5, p. 368 (Table 29-A)
Questions.Explanation: Readability scale: R1=Unreadable, R2=Barely readable, R3=Readable with difficulty, R4=Readable practically no difficulty, R5=Perfectly readable.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: Which ITU Region includes Ireland, Europe, Africa, and the former Soviet Union?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 20.2, p. 314
Questions.Explanation: ITU Region 1 covers Europe, Africa, the Middle East, and northern Asia. (Region 2 = Americas; Region 3 = Asia-Pacific).

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What is the official ITU emission designator for full double-sideband AM voice?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 20.6, p. 317
Questions.Explanation: A3E = Double sideband AM voice telephony.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: What call sign format must an Irish licensee (e.g. EI8XYZ) use while visiting England under CEPT T/R 61-01?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.3, p. 322 & Ch 21.4, p. 324 / Sample Exam Q56
Questions.Explanation: The visitor prepends the host country prefix (M for England) separated by a stroke: M/EI8XYZ.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: Can an Irish HAREC certificate be used to apply for a permanent amateur licence when taking up residence in another CEPT country?
Options: No, you must re-take the host country's exam in their native language
Only after living in the host country for 5 years
Only if you hold a Class 1 Morse license
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.1, p. 320
Questions.Explanation: T/R 61-02 allows holders moving permanently to a participating CEPT nation to obtain a local equivalent license without re-examination.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Question: Has the United States adopted CEPT Recommendation T/R 61-01 for temporary visitors?
Options: Only if paying a $100 registration fee
No, the USA does not recognize CEPT licences
Yes, but only for Morse code on 40m
Yes, US FCC permits CEPT Class 1 holders to operate in the US as short-term visitors using W/ or K/ prefixes
Questions.Correct answer: Yes, US FCC permits CEPT Class 1 holders to operate in the US as short-term visitors using W/ or K/ prefixes
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 21.1, p. 320 (Footnote 390)
Questions.Explanation: The USA adopted T/R 61-01 (short visits), but has NOT adopted T/R 61-02 for issuing permanent US licenses.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.10 Irish Laws, Regulations, and Licence Conditions
Questions.Question: Under what circumstances can ComReg suspend or revoke an amateur station licence?
Options: In the event of serious or repeated non-compliance with licence conditions
If the licensee fails to make 100 contacts per year
If the licensee operates on 20m during nighttime
If the licensee changes their antenna type
Questions.Correct answer: In the event of serious or repeated non-compliance with licence conditions
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.4, p. 328
Questions.Explanation: ComReg may suspend or revoke a licence for serious or repeated non-compliance with statutory regulations or licence terms.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.10 Irish Laws, Regulations, and Licence Conditions
Questions.Question: What mark indicates that commercially manufactured radio transmitting equipment meets EU safety and EMC standards?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.12, p. 332
Questions.Explanation: The CE type approval mark indicates compliance with EU RED, EMC, and electrical safety directives.

Questions.Section: Section B: Operating Rules, Procedures, Regulations
Questions.Subsection: B.10 Irish Laws, Regulations, and Licence Conditions
Questions.Question: What maximum power is permitted for land mobile (/M) operation on HF primary bands (80m, 40m, 20m, 15m, 10m) in Ireland?
Questions.Source: IRTS HAREC Study Guide Ch 22.7, p. 329
Questions.Explanation: Land mobile (/M) operation on primary HF bands is limited to 100W PEP (20 dBW).
